get.description:
The application server key a browser needs to subscribe.

Public by construction - it is handed to every subscribing browser - but
absent when the server has no keys, so the client can say push is
unavailable rather than failing mid-permission-prompt.

Redacted on purpose: an endpoint is a capability, not a display field.

`device_hash` is the SHA-256 of the caller's own push endpoint, which lets
the response mark which row is the device in the parent's hand without ever
returning an endpoint. A hash cannot be sent to, so it is safe in a query
string in a way the endpoint itself would not be.

post.description:
Queue a test notification to this adult's devices.

Deliberately goes through the same outbox and drain a real notification
uses, rather than sending inline. A test that took a different path would
prove that the different path works, which is not the question a parent is
asking when they press the button.

Accepted, not sent: the drain picks it up on its next pass.

Issue a feed, replacing any existing one.

The response carries the raw token. It is the only time it exists outside
the parent's calendar client, and the surface showing it must say so:
regenerating invalidates the previous URL, and every device that already
subscribed has to add the new one.

put.description:
Change what reaches the calendar, without changing the URL.

Deliberately not a regeneration: a parent adjusting what appears should not
have to re-add the calendar on every device.
